nodes.name: ZIF-67@CoFe2O4 nanosheets growth
nodes.procedure: ZIF-67@CoFeOx nanosheets were uniformly grown on the FF by a simple liquid phase precipitation method at room temperature (RT) for 5 h according to the previously reported method with partially modified. Detailed: First, 0.873 g Co(NO3)2·6H2O was dissolved in 55 mL DI to form Co solution, and 1.64 g 2-MI was dissolved in 50 mL DI to form 2-MI solution. Second, Co solution was poured into 2-MI solution to form purple ZIF-67 solution; then a slice of Fe foam (2×2 cm²) was immersed in the purple ZIF-67 solution. After stirring for 30 min, purple ZIF-67 solution was allowed to stand for 5 h at RT.

nodes.name: Washing, drying, and phosphorization
nodes.procedure: Third, the precursor loaded onto the Fe foam was washed 3 times with ethanol and DI, and dried at 50°C overnight. Finally, the dried sample (ZIF-67@CoFe2O4/FF) was put in downstream of the tube furnace, and NaH2PO2 was placed in upstream. Phosphating was carried out at 350°C under an Ar gas flow for 2 h to form the C@CoP-FeP/FF electrodes.

nodes.characterization_summary: C@CoP-FeP/FF presents nanosheet array morphology with abundant porous structure and flower-like microstructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of CoFeP/FF and C@CoP-FeP/FF were shown in Figure 1b-g. ... Different from CoFeP/FF, the C@CoP-FeP/FF presents a nanosheet array morphology with abundant porous structure due to the introduction of carbon.

nodes.characterization_summary: C@CoP-FeP/FF shows porous structure protected by ultrathin carbon layer (0.8-4.3 nm thick). Lattice spacings of 0.21 nm and 0.27 nm ascribed to (201) and (211) planes of FeP; 0.26 nm and 0.29 nm to (211) and (103) planes of CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c further demonstrates that the CoP-FeP nanosheets have been well protected by an ultrathin carbon layer, with a thickness of 0.8-4.3 nm. ... As presented in Figure 2d, the lattice spacings of 0.21 and 0.27 nm can be ascribed to (201) and (211) crystallographic planes of FeP.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pore size distributions of C@CoP-FeP mainly range from 3 to 24 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pore structure of C@CoP-FeP was further characterized by Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analysis. As presented in Figure S5, Supporting Information, the pore size distributions mainly range from 3 to 24 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: C@CoP-FeP/FF shows Co 2p peaks for Co²⁺ (784.14/802.11 eV), Co³⁺ (781.93/798.34 eV), Co-P (778.92/793.85 eV); Fe 2p peaks at 722.96 eV, 713.61 eV, Fe-P at 709.80 eV; P 2p M-P peak at 129.34 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a shows the XPS spectra of the two electrodes, confirming the existence of Co, Fe, P, C, and N in the C@CoP-FeP/FF electrode... The Co 2p spectra of C@CoP-FeP/FF present three pairs of peaks corresponding to the Co²⁺ (784.14/802.11 eV), Co³⁺ (781.93/798.34 eV), and Co-P bond (778.92/793.85 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: C@CoP-FeP/FF has double layer capacitance Cdl of 31.76 mF cm⁻² in 1 M KOH (higher than CoFeP/FF at 27.05 mF cm⁻²). In simulated seawater, Cdl is 70.31 mF cm⁻² (higher than CoFeP/FF at 43.36 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S10, Supporting Information, the electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) value of C@CoP-FeP/FF (31.76 mF cm⁻²) is higher than those of FF (12.05 mF cm⁻²) and CoFeP/FF (27.05 mF cm⁻²). ... in simulated seawater, the ECSA value of C@CoP-FeP/FF (70.31 mF cm⁻²) is higher than those of FF (18.29 mF cm⁻²) and CoFeP/FF (43.36 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: C@CoP-FeP/FF shows series resistance Rs of 2.4 Ω and smallest charge transfer resistance Rct.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As Figure S12, Supporting Information, shows, the C@CoP-FeP/FF presents a series resistance (Rs) of 2.4Ω and the smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct), suggesting a favorable charge transport ability of C@CoP-FeP/FF.
